body:
Customers don’t buy in straight lines. They change dates and budgets, have questions halfway and expect the answer to come with the next step. Forms and filters make them start over. A voice AI assistant does not. It searches, answers, adapts and completes the transaction in a single conversation.

In our recent webinar, Pieter Peeters (GTM), Boning Gong (FDE) and Shana Inch (GTM) showed how an AI agent built on ElevenAgents handles real hotel booking conversations, what separates agents that perform from agents that disappoint and how teams get from pilot to production.

## Key takeaways

• One conversation replaces forms and filters. Customers change dates, budgets and plans mid-request. The AI assistant searches live data, adapts, and completes the booking or order. At Rohlik , customers can already search products, build a shopping list and check out by voice.

• A good assistant guides, not only answers. It knows the customer and the catalogue. In our demo, the assistant caught a clash with an earlier booking that the customer had forgotten. At Immobiliare.it , a listing assistant lifted lead qualification 3.3x.

• Support follows the same pattern . Customers with a problem want it solved, not routed. Rohlik’s assistant, Maia, handles 90% of incoming hotline calls, and Klarna’s assistant is first-line phone support for all 35 million US customers.

• Voice earns its place as conversations get harder. Past two minutes, voice succeeds 29% more often than chat. In our study, 85% of 98 people preferred voice over chat to rebook a cancelled flight. Speed matters too: a 16% drop in latency came with a 26% rise in success.

• Configuration decides the outcome. Many AI agents that disappoint are set up wrong: the wrong model, the wrong voice or too little time spent on configuration. Technology is not the problem. Building with a forward deployed engineer or a trained partner gets far more out of the project.

## Why customers want an assistant, not a form

Customers don't book or buy in straight lines. A request starts as two nights near the canals, becomes three, then runs into a trip already on the calendar. In a shop, a basket starts with a recipe, grows with the usual order and ends at checkout. Forms and filters are too static for that. Each change forces the customer to start over or leave. Each change forces the customer to start over or leave, which is part of why 70% of online carts, checkouts and bookings are abandoned.

Choosing is the hard part. Few customers know which filter to set. They know what they want: a quiet hotel near the museums under €400 a night, a recipe for four, a home close to the school. A good assistant asks the next question, narrows the options and recommends one. It also knows the customer.

Support follows the same pattern. A customer with a problem does not want a phone menu or a queue. They want it solved, in their own language, and handed to a person with the full context when the assistant cannot do it. Demand also ignores office hours. At SevenRooms, 1 in 5 of the calls handled by its Voice AI arrived after hours. Voicemail doesn't catch them: 80% of callers who reach it hang up without leaving a message. US data from the Marchex Institute shows that 1 in 7 phone calls fails, unanswered or abandoned.

## The cost of unanswered calls

Stress pushes people toward voice. In an ElevenLabs study of 98 people, 85% preferred voice over chat to rebook a cancelled flight, and named speed of resolution and empathy among their top reasons. Chat works for short questions, but across hundreds of production agents running both channels, voice succeeds 29% more often once a conversation runs past two minutes. Many teams automate chat or email first and add voice last. In our experience, starting with voice lifts metrics right away.

## Voice excels in complex customer conversations

## What AI retail assistants deliver in production

AI assistants pay off first where customers need help choosing, ordering or fixing something: a shop with a long catalogue, a booking site with too many filters, a support queue that keeps growing. ElevenAgents is live across hospitality, travel, retail, commerce and marketplaces, and customers have published results in five areas.

Capturing demand outside opening hours. SevenRooms Voice AI, powered by ElevenAgents, has handled more than 400,000 calls across 600+ restaurants, 1 in 5 of them after hours. Restaurants captured up to 25% more reservations, based on SevenRooms data comparing venues' first three months on Voice AI in 2026 with the same period a year earlier.

Resolving support faster, in the customer's channel and language. Rohlik Group , one of Europe's largest online grocery platforms, serves 3 million customers across five countries. Its agent, Maia, handles 90% of incoming hotline calls and 90% of customer communications across phone, web, app and WhatsApp, in six languages. Resolution is over 2x faster and available 24/7, and Rohlik is on track to cut operational costs by 50% while maintaining CSAT. Customers can also search products, build a list and check out by voice. "We believe voice is the future of grocery," says Lukas Honke, Head of AI Engineering at Rohlik Group. Klarna runs its agent as first-line phone support for all 35 million US customers, with resolutions up to 10x faster for the queries it handles. eDreams ODIGEO reports double-digit improvements in resolution speed and in transfer rates across five languages, and LOT Polish Airlines is deploying ElevenAgents for inbound phone support, including booking changes and ticket inquiries.

Getting local languages right. KPN built Mobiel AI, an assistant inside its business mobile plans. Joint work took Dutch verification accuracy from roughly 50% to 90%, and that improvement now benefits every Dutch-language deployment on the platform.
